start.text: As you step off the road, the pinned moth lifts from the signpost and unfolds into a narrow man in a grey felt coat. He bows, then bows again, a degree deeper than the first. 'Thistlewick, herald of the Court of Moths. You carry a shard and a letter, and the Lady has been waiting some time to see which of the world's fools would bring them.'
start.speaker: whisperwood_thistlewick

choices.text: Bow, properly and exactly as deep as his.
[Deception] 'The Queen sent me. Naturally.'
[Insight] Watch what he leaves unsaid.
'Take me to your Lady. Now.'

polite.speaker: whisperwood_thistlewick
polite.text: 'Charming. Rare, even.' He straightens, visibly pleased. 'Follow the Mothlight Path. Do not leave it, do not eat what you are offered, and do not thank anyone for anything. Be as rude as you like in the honest way. We are quite used to that.'

smooth.speaker: whisperwood_thistlewick
smooth.text: His eyebrows climb a quarter inch. 'The Queen, you say. How interesting.' He does not say he believes you; he does not say he doesn't. 'Come, then. We shall see whether the Lady is as easily charmed as I.'

caught.speaker: whisperwood_thistlewick
caught.text: 'No, I do not think so.' He says it kindly, which is worse. 'But you amuse me, which is the next best thing. The Lady will have a word about it.' The leaves overhead rustle with something very like laughter.

read.speaker: whisperwood_thistlewick
read.text: You notice that he never says the word 'dead'. When he mentions the Queen, his hand drifts to the moth pinned on his hat and touches it twice. He is grieving, and trying very hard to be correct about it. 'Come, please,' he says, with an old courtesy over something raw. 'The Lady will see you.'

curt.speaker: whisperwood_thistlewick
curt.text: 'Of course. Impatience is a quality in the young.' His smile never moves. 'The Mothlight Path, then. It is shorter than it looks, and rather longer than it feels.'

start.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
start.text: The hall falls silent. Veyra, Lady of Moths, regards you from her throne of white roots with the unhurried interest of a heron regarding a fish. 'A mortal with a letter and a shard,' she says. 'And a warden's coat, if I am not mistaken. How very small you are. How very quick.'

choices.text: Bow, exactly as Thistlewick taught you.
Bow, clumsily.
[Persuasion] Greet her as an equal, and mean it.
[Deception] 'I speak for the Queen herself.'

equal.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
equal.text: A ripple passes through the courtiers. 'Mm.' The Lady leans back. 'Few say it so plainly. Few say it plainly at all.' Something almost like warmth touches her mouth. 'Very well, my equal. Sit. Let us speak of what we want from one another.'

cold.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
cold.text: 'No,' she says gently. 'Not yet. You are very new.' The courtiers murmur, a sound like dry leaves. 'But we shall speak. Come closer.'

envoy.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
envoy.text: Her eyes narrow, then widen with delight. 'A lie, and a good one. The Queen did not send you. The Queen sent no one for four months.' Her voice drops, grave. 'But you have more courage than most of my courtiers. Sit.'

caught.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
caught.text: 'Do not lie to me in my own hall.' It is not loud. Every lantern in the hall dims. 'I let it pass because I am curious, not because I am fooled. Do it again, and the stair will not remember you.'

terms.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
terms.text: 'The Queen gave us a shard,' says the Lady. 'She asked us to keep it from mortal hands. You are a mortal hand, and yet you bring the miller's piece and the miller's letter, and the Wood speaks of you with surprising kindness. So. We trade. My Court's mothlamp, which lights our longest night, was carried north by one of our Wardens. The cold took him, and now he keeps the light for himself. Bring it back, and I will weigh a bargain for the shard.'

choices.text: 'I'll bring it back.'
[Insight] 'Why did the Queen leave it here, and not with her own guards?'
[History] 'What exactly is the heart-stone?'
'Could I buy it? I have gold.'
'I won't fetch your lamp. Give me the shard.'

accept.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
accept.text: 'Wise.' She lifts one hand, and a moth drifts down from the rafters to settle on your sleeve. It will lead you to the clearing, and then it will die. 'It is a small thing. I ask you to remember that. Come back when the lamp is in your hands, and we will speak of bargains.'

effects.message: A grey moth rests on your sleeve. It will guide you north, to the briar-choked clearing.

why.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
why.text: She is quiet for several breaths. 'Because her guards were not hers. Because someone in the capital was pulling the strings of every man she trusted.' The room feels colder. 'She was afraid, Wanderer. Not of dying. Of being used. She is the only person I have ever seen choose not to be.'

stone.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
stone.text: 'A summer sealed in a stone. The first king who held it kept the northern cold from waking. The stone is cracked now; the cold is waking.' She says it as one reads a ledger. 'The Thornwake is not an army, small mortal. It is a season that has forgotten how to end.'

deflect.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
deflect.text: 'That is a question for another day, and a better asker.' She smiles, faintly. 'The lamp, mortal. The lamp first.'

gold.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
gold.text: Her laugh is a single, bell-like note. 'Gold! What would I do with it? Count it? Wear it?' Several courtiers titter. 'No. I want what is mine, and what is mine is a lamp. Bring it.'

refuse.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
refuse.text: 'Then you may leave with nothing, small mortal, or you may try your luck with the reliquary.' She does not point at it. 'I do not recommend the second. But I observe that nobody has ever forbidden me from being curious about what you do.' She turns her face away, dismissing you.

effects.message: The Lady has neither forbidden nor invited you to take what she holds. She has noticed the pearly coffer behind her throne, and that you have noticed it too.

start.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
start.text: The lamp burns steadily in the Lady's hands, and the hall seems to breathe out. Then she sets it on its hook above the throne, turns, and opens the pearly coffer. The moth shard lies on silk, pale gold and humming. 'A bargain, then. The Court gives you this. In return, the Court asks two things. First, that you do not tell the Regency, or any crowned head, where this Court sits. Second, that when the Crown is whole again, you return one night's light of the stone to the Wood, which has paid dearly for the cold. Will you swear it, in the old way?'

choices.text: 'I swear it.' Mean it, and say so.
[Persuasion] 'The first, gladly. The second, I cannot promise. Let me swear what I can keep.'
[Deception] Swear it with a straight face, and plan to break it.
[Intimidation] 'You'll hand it over, or I'll take it.'
'I need to think about it.'

kept.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
kept.text: She speaks the words, and you speak them back. A bell rings from the depths of the Wood, and every lantern in the hall flickers as one. Something cold and bright settles over your shoulders and is gone. 'It is done,' says Veyra. 'It is binding, small mortal. I will remember. So will the Wood.' She presses the shard into your palm. It is warm now.

effects.message: The Court of Moths has taken your oath. The shard is warm in your hand.

haggle.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
haggle.text: The Lady's eyebrows rise, a full inch. 'Honest in your limits. I have not met that in a mortal in a hundred years.' She considers. 'The first, then, and the second softened: that you will carry a single pressed moth to the Crown's forging and let it be seen. A small thing.' She holds out the shard. 'Swear, and be the first mortal to haggle with me and win.'

haggle_fail.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
haggle_fail.text: 'No.' It is gentle and total. 'You wish the shard and not the price. The Court does not sell cheaper than it values.' She closes the coffer. 'Return when you can say yes, or return when you cannot help but say no. Either answer, I will hear.'

lie.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
lie.text: You say it smoothly, and the bell tolls. She presses the shard into your hand, and for the space of a heartbeat her eyes rest on your face with the faintest, saddest curiosity. 'You will keep that, I think,' she says. 'Or you will not. It is, as always, a mortal's choice.' She knows. She says nothing, and the silence is heavier than anything she could say.

caught.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
caught.text: The bell does not ring. The Lady's face does not change. 'You do not mean it,' she says. 'Not a word of it.' The sentinels stir. 'Go. Return when you are brave enough to be honest, or foolish enough to try again.'

fear.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
fear.text: The Lady is silent a long, long while. 'I see,' she says at last. 'A mortal that can look at me and not blink.' She takes the shard and drops it in your palm as one drops a coin in a beggar's cup. 'Take it, then. But a bargain refused is a bargain remembered. The Wood will not forget.'

duel.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
duel.text: 'Sir Gossamer,' says the Lady, without raising her voice. The tall knight steps forward from the pillars and draws a rapier like a splinter of night. 'Mortal. If you wish to take what is ours, you may take it from him.' The harp stops playing.

effects.message: Sir Gossamer bows to you, perfectly, and the duel begins.

farewell.speaker: whisperwood_veyra
farewell.text: She watches you go, a pale shape in a hall of a thousand tiny lamps. 'Salt and smugglers, Wanderer,' she says at your back. 'The next piece went south, to a fence who has never met a secret he would not sell. Follow the scent of brine.'

start.text: You ask the pool a question. For a long moment nothing moves. Then the surface darkens, as though a cloud had passed over a sky that is not there, and a voice speaks from just below the water, in a whisper that sounds almost like your own.

choices.text: Ask what the Court wants with the shard.
Ask what you are most afraid of.
[Arcana] Ask what the pool is made of.
Leave the pool alone.

court.text: 'They want to keep their promise,' the voice says. 'To a girl who is not there. They want it very much. They are afraid they will not be able to.' The ripples settle. That is all.

fear.text: The pool shows you a corridor. At the end of it a door stands open on a field of snow, and someone you love is walking away across the white. You call out. They do not turn. The water goes still and shows you only your own tired face. 'Walk faster,' says the voice, not unkindly.

made.text: 'Of the first rain,' the voice answers, amused, 'and every face that ever leaned over it.' The pool ripples. Somewhere under the surface, hundreds of reflections turn their heads at once. 'Do not stay long. We are fond of faces.'

silence.text: The water offers nothing but a ripple, and the faint impression of a smile.
